requests.author: luissiviero
requests.body:
Request changes on PR #152 (build(0002)). Gate (c) parked on the capped run's wall clock, not on the code; this round resets the clock and settles the reviewer's open `escalate` and a fresh-context review of the diff. Fix them in the files plan.md already lists, with a test each; no change to spec.md (choice 164), plan.md only where a step or the file list changes.

1. `plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py` `_part_targets`, the git branch: the subcommand is read at a fixed position (`words[1]`) with no flag-skipping, so a git global option before the verb hides the write — `git -c core.fileMode=false rm CLAUDE.md`, `git --git-dir=.git rm CLAUDE.md`, `git --work-tree=. checkout -- CLAUDE.md` all yield no candidate (`shell_write_targets` returns `[]`; `git rm CLAUDE.md` returns `['CLAUDE.md']`). Skip git's global options before the verb the way `cp`/`mv`/`rm` skip flags (`_nonflag`), consuming the argument of `-c`, `-C`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `--namespace` and `--exec-path` when it is a separate token; a test per form, and the same forms in the `-C` resolution path (`_git_dash_c`), which must still see `-C <dir>` when another global option precedes it.
2. `_inner_shell_command`: only the adjacent pair (`bash`, `-c`) is recognised, so an interpreter flag between the program and `-c` skips the recursion — `bash --norc -c 'echo x > CLAUDE.md'`, `sh --posix -c '…'`, `pwsh -NoProfile -Command '…'`, `cmd /d /c '…'` are never parsed inside, while `bash -c 'echo x > CLAUDE.md'` yields `CLAUDE.md`. Find the `-c`/`/c`/`-Command` token after any flags, recurse into the next token; a test per interpreter.

3. `_part_targets` and `decide()`: a directory target never matches a protected pattern (`/.claude/**` needs a slash after `.claude`; `docs/policy.md` does not match `docs`), so a recursive delete or move of a guardrail directory, or of an ancestor of a `protected_paths` entry, is allowed — `python -c "import shutil; shutil.rmtree('.claude')"`, `git rm -r -q .claude`, `git rm -r -q docs`, `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force .claude` all `allow` (reproduced on a scratch project with `docs/policy.md` under `protected_paths`); `shutil.rmtree` is on the spec's own idiom list. Deny a resolved target that is an ancestor of a protected pattern's fixed prefix or of the plugin root; a test with the four forms.
4. The two-argument interpreter calls check the source, not the destination: `shutil.copy('README.md','CLAUDE.md')` yields the candidate `README.md` and is allowed; the same for `os.replace`, `os.rename`, `shutil.move`, node `copyFileSync`/`renameSync`/`cpSync` and `[IO.File]::Copy`/`Move`. Take the last literal (the destination), as the `cp`/`mv` branch already does; a parametrized row per call.
5. Python `open` write forms the regex misses, each `[]`: `open('CLAUDE.md', mode='w')`, a mode in a variable (`m='w'; open('CLAUDE.md', m)` — fail closed), `open(r'CLAUDE.md','w')`, `Path('CLAUDE.md').open('w')`, `os.open('CLAUDE.md', os.O_WRONLY|os.O_TRUNC)`. One idiom row each.
6. PowerShell paths are mangled by the POSIX backslash escape: with `tool_name: PowerShell`, `Set-Content .\CLAUDE.md x` becomes the candidate `.CLAUDE.md` and is allowed, `Set-Content 'CLAUDE.md' x` is denied, and an unquoted `C:\…\CLAUDE.md` loses every backslash. `.\path` is the ordinary PowerShell spelling on the owner's platform. Keep `\` literal when the tool is PowerShell (its escape is the backtick); a test `test_shell_guard_reads_a_backslash_path_on_powershell`.
7. `_powershell_targets` takes the wrong positional when a named parameter precedes the path: `Set-Content -Value x CLAUDE.md` → `x`, `"x" | Out-File -Encoding utf8 CLAUDE.md` → `utf8`, `Set-Content -Path:CLAUDE.md -Value x` (the colon form is not parsed), `New-Item -ItemType File CLAUDE.md` → `File` — all allowed. Skip the value of every `-Name value` pair when looking for the positional, split `-Param:value`; the four rows.
8. The directory-change parser takes `words[1]` as the directory even when it is a flag or a special word: `cd -P .claude && python -c 1 > settings.json` resolves under `<root>/-P/` and is allowed (the write lands in `.claude/settings.json`); `cd docs && cd - && echo x > CLAUDE.md` is allowed; `Set-Location -Path .claude; Set-Content settings.json x` allowed; `sl` is not in `_CD_WORDS`; `pushd … && popd && …` resolves to the wrong directory. Skip flags; add `sl`, `chdir`, `Push-Location`; fail closed on `cd -`, a bare `cd`, `popd` and `Pop-Location`; and add the `pushd` and `Set-Location` resolution tests spec.md Acceptance names (today absent — which is how this went unseen).
9. Shell structure hides the head word, so the git, PowerShell and `cp`-style branches never fire: `git status & git rm -q CLAUDE.md` (a lone `&` is not a separator), `(git rm -q CLAUDE.md)`, `{ git rm -q CLAUDE.md; }`, `if true; then git rm -q CLAUDE.md; fi`, `GIT_TRACE=0 git rm -q CLAUDE.md` (an assignment prefix), `(cd .claude && python -c 1 > settings.json)` — all `[]`, all allowed, each confirmed in bash to delete or write the file. Split on a lone `&`; strip a leading `(`, `{`, `!`, `then`, `do`, `else` and `NAME=value` words and a trailing `)`; a test `test_shell_write_targets_sees_through_subshells_groups_and_assignments`.
10. `_strip_heredocs` matches `<<WORD` anywhere in a line, inside quotes and in a here-string, and then drops every later line: `git log -1 --format='<<EOF'` followed on the next line by `git rm -q CLAUDE.md` yields `[]`, and `python -c 1 <<< "x"` followed by the same does too (`<<<` read as `<<"x"`); bash ran the second line. Detect heredocs in the quote-aware tokenizer and exclude `<<<`; a test that line 2's `git rm CLAUDE.md` is still seen in both forms.
11. The non-literal rule misses brace expansion and git pathspec magic: `git rm -q {CLAUDE,README}.md` is allowed (bash removed both files), `git rm -q ':(icase)claude.md'` and `':/CLAUDE.md'` are allowed (git removed `CLAUDE.md`). Add `{` to `_NONLITERAL_RE` and fail closed on a git path argument that starts with `:`; the two fail-closed rows.
12. `>&WORD` is not parsed as a file redirect: `python -c 1 >&CLAUDE.md` gives the candidate `&CLAUDE.md` and is allowed (bash wrote the file). Parse `>&WORD` as a redirect when WORD is neither a digit nor `-`; an idiom row.
13. Options of the allowed programs that write a named file are not idioms, so in CI — where the hook's surface is exactly these programs — each is allowed: `git diff --output=CLAUDE.md` (wrote a 117-byte diff into it), `git checkout main CLAUDE.md` (no `--`), `git config --file sdlc.yaml a.b c`, `python -m json.tool x.json sdlc.yaml` (wrote it), `python -m pytest --basetemp=.claude` (deleted `.claude/settings.json`), `gh release download … -O CLAUDE.md`. Add them as idioms with one row each, plus a negative row proving the framework's own `git diff --stat --patch --output=changes/<id>-<slug>/evidence/diff-c.patch` stays allowed (it resolves under `changes/`).
14. Git Bash absolute paths (`/c/Users/…/CLAUDE.md`) fall outside a `C:/…` root (`rel_to` returns `None`) and are allowed while the `C:/` spelling is denied — read in the code, not reproduced here (needs a drive-letter root). Map `/x/…` to `x:/…` in `_resolve` when the root has a drive letter; a test with root `C:/p` and target `/c/p/CLAUDE.md`.
15. **A false denial that parks ordinary runs**: the interpreter-literal scan reads every part's raw text, quotes included, so `git commit -m "deny open('CLAUDE.md','w') via Bash"`, `gh pr comment 144 --body "… fs.writeFileSync('sdlc.yaml','x') …"` and `grep -n "open('CLAUDE.md','w')" tests/test_hooks.py` are each denied with the "Protected path … Stop and report" reason (reproduced: `BLOCK`) — this change's own commit messages, fix responses and review comments quote exactly these strings. Scan only the code argument of `python -c`/`python3 -c`/`node -e`/`pwsh -Command`; add the three commands to `test_shell_guard_allows_ordinary_commands`. The same for a `#` comment (`git status # then > CLAUDE.md` is denied): strip an unquoted comment.
16. PowerShell `$null` fails closed as a non-literal target: `git fetch origin 2>$null` and `python -m pytest > $null` with `tool_name: PowerShell` are denied ("not a literal path") — the PowerShell spelling of `> /dev/null`, which the spec's negative list allows. Treat `$null` as the null device; the two rows on the allowed list.
17. `tests/test_ci.py` (the one pre-existing assertion the plan permits to change, decision 1 of the third design review): `data["sandbox"] == source["sandbox"]` became equality on `network` plus the `denyWrite` list, so `enabled`, `failIfUnavailable` and `allowUnsandboxedCommands` are no longer asserted on the rendered copy (reproduced: a copy with the three keys dropped passes the updated assertions). Restore full equality with only `filesystem.denyWrite` substituted: `data["sandbox"] == {**source["sandbox"], "filesystem": {"denyWrite": [...]}}`.

**Nits, for the same round where cheap** (the reviewer's reading, not reproduced here):

18. `decide()` looks the test-file lock up on every shell command, even with no write candidate, and fails closed when it cannot read the change folder — on a `sdlc/<id>/c` branch of a project whose change folder is missing, `git status` is denied. Look the lock up only when there is at least one candidate; a test.
19. A denial is logged before it is emitted: with a hung git the log's own git call makes a block take 40 s against the hook's 30 s timeout, and a timed-out PreToolUse hook does not block (NOTES §8). Emit first, or pass `default_path` so the log needs no git call.
20. `_deny_write_entries` (`plugin/ci/run_phase.py`): a non-list `protected_paths` (`protected_paths: docs/x.md`) is iterated character by character and yields the project root itself, as does `- .`, so the whole project becomes `denyWrite`; `../outside.txt` is not normalised; a bare name (`policy.md`, which the hook protects in every directory) narrows silently to the root copy and is not noted under `_denyWriteSkipped`. Reject a non-list, drop an entry that resolves to the root or outside it, note bare names; rows in the `ci_settings_file` test.
21. `tests/test_hooks.py:22` imports `shell_guard` at module top (plan step 1: inside the tests); the wiring test does not assert `timeout == 30`.

Not asked for here (0.3.x candidates, recorded in PROGRESS "Session 24"): `_absolute_rule_root` now used by tests only; `tests/test_evals.py:519` `names == list(FRAMEWORK_SUITE)` is tautological (both sides from `run.discover`; the names are still asserted by key); the `run_hook` exception path logs nothing on a fail-closed crash.

requests.body:
Request changes on PR #152 (build(0002)), gate (e). The round resets the counter and settles the review pass's one Important finding and two of its nits; no change to spec.md (choice 164).

1. `tests/test_hooks.py:22` imports `shell_guard` at module scope. plan.md step 1 and its files-that-change entry say the import goes inside each test, so a failure in the new tests cannot abort collection of the rest of the file. Move the import inside the tests as the plan says (do not change plan.md to match the diff); keep the `timeout == 30` assertion in the wiring test.
2. `plugin/ci/run_phase.py:1081` `_absolute_rule_root` has no production caller since `ci_settings_file` calls `_posix_root` directly; only `tests/test_ci.py` uses it. Remove it and the test lines that call it.
3. `tests/test_evals.py:519` `names == list(FRAMEWORK_SUITE)` compares two calls of the same discovery against each other. Assert against a literal list of the case folder names so a skipped or duplicated case is caught.

The 985-line length of `plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py` is accepted for this change; a split is a 0.3.x candidate.
